research_rationale:
Executive Order 13561 sets pay rates for the statutory pay systems, the Senior Executive Service, executive, legislative and judicial salaries, uniformed services, locality payments and administrative law judges by attached schedules, and in its last section supersedes its predecessor. Section 8 of the later Executive Order 13594 says that Executive Order 13561 'is superseded' without a qualifying effective-date clause, and the later order was signed on 2011-12-19. That express supersession of the whole order is recorded as the first end of every clause. The later order's section 7 gives its own schedules effective dates, and for the Schedule 8 and other schedules those dates may precede the signing date; this is disclosed as a note for the reviewer. A search of held order texts for the number 13561 finds the later order, and the later order is the earliest held instrument naming this one.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Express supersession by Executive Order 13594 section 8, signed 2011-12-19, is the first end found; held texts that cite the number 13561 show no earlier revocation or supersession.","independent_command_check":"No clause is independent of the schedules; the implementing direction to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management and the statutory pay-rate commands all fall with the supersession of the whole order.","savings_check":"Pay already accrued under the schedules for pay periods before the later order's effective dates is an accrued consequence; the later order has no saving clause.","scope_check":"Every section and lettered paragraph of the original is a separate clause and each is ended by the same supersession of the whole order."}

savings.reason: No saving clause appears in the later order; pay accrued under the superseded schedules before the later schedules took effect is an accrued consequence, not a continuing command.
